body.statement:
For every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\), there is a one-copy structural compiler \(\mathscr A\) with the following properties. It rejects any cell rank exceeding two. A rank-two cell is represented by its two oriented segment modes, refined by all coefficient-support faces. A rank-one cell is represented by the disjoint \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes of \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\), with the \(\mathrm E\) split refined coordinatewise. Products of the four local modes use one shared variable \(b_i\) at each response vertex, fix proxy supports, and retain endpoint equalities and inequalities, observed-line incidences, and guarded nonzero pivots as polynomial sign atoms. Writing \(X_\chi\) for the resulting charts, their union is exactly \(\mathcal C_A(T)\). In design B, adjoining \(\rho\), the zero-residual or active negatively proportional state at every response type, lexicographic nonzero pivots, forest propagation, the active-cycle product-one constraint, positive component scales, normalization, and a signed relevance witness gives a finite chart union exactly equal to \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).

In design A, before declaring compatibility or attempting a lift, \(\mathscr A\) tests \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\). After that test, and directly in design B, it tests all structural charts for emptiness. If all are empty, it reports incompatibility. Otherwise it obtains one semialgebraic sample \(x_0\) in the nonempty union, sets \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\), and for every chart \(X_\chi\) tests existential realizability of
\[
 X_\chi\cap\left\{x:
 (\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1})^2+
 (\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2})^2>0\right\}. \tag{2}
\]
The global target image is the singleton \(\{t_0\}\) if and only if every refinement in (2) is empty. A nonempty refinement directly supplies a point \(x_1\) with \(\tau_C(x_1)\neq\tau_C(x_0)\), and the full-SCM lift supplies legal target-changing twins. Connected-component descriptions may be returned as optional diagnostics but are not used by the rigidity decision. The computation uses no generic two-copy unequal-target predicate. Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), termination is relative to effective arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles. A target is reported as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when that expression is actually constructed; otherwise it is reported by a real-univariate representation and Thom sign data over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).
body.justification: This theorem proves the exhaustive structural union and a global constancy test from one sampled target and all one-copy chart refinements.
body.gap: The prior compiler paid for connected-component descriptions and target projection even though global disagreement is equivalent to one unequal-target feasibility test per chart.
body.consumer: The atlas and complexity theorem receive an exact one-sample/all-chart classifier with direct legal witness extraction.
body.proof_tex:
We first prove that the structural charts are exhaustive, including every support face. Positivity of the selected table gives \(v_e(z)>0\) for every cell \(e\) and instrument value \(z\). If \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\), the defining equality
\[
 T_e=b_i a_{ei}^{\top}+b_j a_{ej}^{\top} \tag{3}
\]
expresses \(T_e\) as a sum of two rank-one matrices. Hence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(T_e)\leq 2 \tag{4}
\]
at every point of either cycle fiber. A cell rank exceeding two therefore makes every chart, and hence the relevant cycle fiber, empty. Rank zero is impossible because every entry of \(T_e\) is positive.

Fix a rank-two cell. Since \(v_e(z)>0\), its normalized columns
\[
 c_{ez}=\frac{T_e(\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)} \tag{5}
\]
are defined. Equation (3) and \(a_{ei}(z)+a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)\) give
\[
 c_{ez}=\lambda_{ez}b_i+(1-\lambda_{ez})b_j,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{ez}=\frac{a_{ei}(z)}{v_e(z)}\in[0,1]. \tag{6}
\]
Rank two forces \(b_i\neq b_j\), so all observed points in (5) and both endpoints lie on one affine line. Conversely, if the endpoints occur on that line and contain every \(c_{ez}\) in their closed segment, choose a coordinate \(h_e\) separating the endpoints. Then the unique coefficients are
\[
 a_{ei}(z)=v_e(z)
 \frac{c_{ez}(h_e)-b_j(h_e)}{b_i(h_e)-b_j(h_e)},
 \qquad
 a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z). \tag{7}
\]
The denominator in (7) is nonzero by the pivot choice, and the segment condition makes both coefficients nonnegative. The two endpoint orders are exactly the orientations proved exhaustive in \(\mathrm{thm:rank\text{-}two\text{-}orientation\text{-}atlas}\). For each \(z\), the positive sum in (6) permits exactly three support alternatives: the first coefficient is zero, the second is zero, or both are positive. These alternatives exhaust every rank-two coefficient face.

For a rank-one cell, \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\) proves that the four \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes are disjoint and exhaustive. In mode \(\mathrm L\), the inactive endpoint \(b_i\) remains unrestricted except for its simplex and shared-vertex constraints; mode \(\mathrm R\) is symmetric. Mode \(\mathrm E\) retains the entire coordinatewise split vector, including its zero, interior, and upper-endpoint faces. Thus coincident endpoints, inactive response rows, and forced zeros are not removed by a rank or division argument.

Take the product of the four local mode lists and use one common endpoint variable \(b_i\) at the two incidences of response type \(i\). Fix the endpoint and coefficient support states counted by the local modes. Every endpoint equality or inequality, line incidence, and pivot condition required by a mode is retained as a polynomial sign atom in that coarse structural template; a remaining finite alternative is retained as a Boolean combination of those atoms rather than counted as a new structural template. A denominator is cleared only after its nonzero sign has been recorded. Equations (6)--(7), the rank-two orientation theorem, and the rank-one normal-form lemma show that every point of \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) belongs to at least one chart. Direct substitution into (3), the endpoint simplex equations, and \(a_{ei}+a_{ej}=v_e\) proves that every chart point belongs to \(\mathcal C_A(T)\). Consequently,
\[
 \bigcup_\chi X_\chi=\mathcal C_A(T). \tag{8}
\]

For design B, fix a chart in (8) and a positive projective vector \(\rho\). At every response type, \(\mathrm{thm:iv\text{-}residual\text{-}forest}\) proves the exhaustive alternatives: both incident residuals vanish; exactly one vanishes, in which case the branch is infeasible; or both are nonzero and negatively proportional. In the active case the first nonzero residual coordinate is a legal pivot, and its two possible signs form a finite refinement. The resulting positive margin ratios propagate from one positive scale on each forest component. If all four links form the cycle, path consistency is equivalent to the single product-one equation. Scale positivity and the margin normalization give all and only the positive margins. Finally, enumerating an ordered pair \(z<z'\) and the sign of
\[
 q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z) \tag{9}
\]
is exhaustive for relevance. The residual-forest theorem therefore yields
\[
 \bigcup_\chi X_\chi=\mathcal C_B(T) \tag{10}
\]
for the design-B refinements.

The supplied population margin does not occur in (8), so cycle feasibility alone cannot certify a design-A full SCM. The first test in the corrected \(\mathrm{def:atlas\text{-}handle}\), together with \(\mathrm{lem:design\text{-}a\text{-}fiber\text{-}nonempty\text{-}criterion}\), gives
\[
 \mathcal F_A(p,m)\neq\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}
 \ \text{and}\ 
 \bigcup_\chi X_\chi\neq\varnothing. \tag{11}
\]
Thus a supplied margin outside the strict interior is reported as incompatible before sampling or lifting. In design B, (10) and the onto part of \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) give
\[
 \mathcal F_B(p)\neq\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bigcup_\chi X_\chi\neq\varnothing. \tag{12}
\]

Assume now that the appropriate union is nonempty. The target map is polynomial in the chart variables because
\[
 \tau_C(b,a)=
 \left(\sum_z a_{11,2}(z),\sum_z a_{00,2}(z)\right). \tag{13}
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{lem:one\text{-}sample\text{-}all\text{-}chart\text{-}rigidity}\) to the finite family in (8) or (10), with \(f=\tau_C\). It first supplies one \(x_0\), then decides exactly the one-copy refinements (2). The lemma proves
\[
 \tau_C\!\left(\bigcup_\chi X_\chi\right)=\{\tau_C(x_0)\}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{every refinement in (2) is empty}. \tag{14}
\]
This comparison is global: a point on a disconnected component or another support face still belongs to some \(X_\chi\) and is tested against the same fixed \(t_0\). Hence connected-component enumeration is unnecessary for the decision.

The initial sample has a real-univariate representation over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), and (13) places \(t_0\) in its real algebraic coordinate field. The refinements are therefore effective over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\). If all are empty, the exact encoding of \(t_0\) is the rigid output. The compiler returns a rational expression over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only if field arithmetic constructs one; otherwise it retains the real-univariate and Thom representation. If a refinement is nonempty, the cited sampler gives \(x_1\) and (2) gives \(\tau_C(x_1)\neq\tau_C(x_0)\). Equations (8) or (10) make both samples legal cycle points, and \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) produces two full SCMs with identical observables and, in design A, the same supplied margins. Each feasibility formula contains only the one variable block \(x\); \(t_0\) is a fixed algebraic coefficient. This proves the theorem.
